alphaCategories.name: Conviction-Weighted Delta (free LLMs cannot compute pct-of-book)
alphaCategories.description: Helm13F is the only marketplace tool that returns institutional position changes weighted by each filer's reported 13F book value. Computing pct-of-book requires (a) current-quarter holdings, (b) prior-quarter holdings, (c) the filer's total 13F book value for both quarters. Free LLMs lack the live 13F XML data and cannot perform deterministic arithmetic. Every Q1-Q6 row carries pctOfBook + convictionTier ('core'≥5% | 'meaningful'≥1% | 'starter'≥0.25% | 'scout'<0.25%) at the contract-locked boundaries.

alphaCategories.name: Curated-Roster Cluster Detection
alphaCategories.description: Q5 (query_superinvestor_cluster_on_ticker) detects when ≥3 curated superinvestors make same-direction moves (new/add) on the same security in the same quarter and computes a clusterSignal with strength = sum(pctOfBookDelta). Requires (i) the curated 22-name roster — free LLMs cannot enumerate this list, (ii) per-filer book values for both quarters, (iii) cross-filer aggregation math. This is the cluster-detection question that drives FinTwit Burry-just-bought-X / Buffett-and-Ackman-both-loaded-up threads — currently produced by hand.

alphaCategories.name: Fuzzy Filer Name → CIK Resolution
alphaCategories.description: Q4 (query_filer_quarter_delta) accepts both 10-digit CIKs ('0001067983') AND fuzzy names ('Burry', 'Ackman', 'Buffett', 'Druckenmiller', 'Coleman'). Resolver uses Levenshtein + token overlap against a curated alias map, returns ambiguous_filer with candidates+confidences when match drops below 0.7. Free LLMs hallucinate manager portfolios; we ground each answer in the resolved CIK plus accession-number provenance for every holding row.

alphaCategories.name: 13F-HR/A Amendment Handling
alphaCategories.description: Filers can supersede a 13F-HR with a 13F-HR/A for the same period. Helm13F tracks supersededByAccession on filings and recomputes deltas using the latest version. Free LLMs do not know which filings were restated; an out-of-date 'Burry sold X' headline can be invalidated by a later amendment. E5 (get_filing) returns supersededByAccession on every filing, and Q4/Q6 implicitly resolve to the latest version before computing deltas.

alphaCategories.name: Per-Fact EDGAR Provenance (zero hallucination)
alphaCategories.description: Every numeric claim in a response carries a sourceRefs[] link to the exact SEC accession that produced it (e.g. 'https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1067983/000119312526054580/'). Buyers can verify every row against EDGAR. Free LLMs return prose without sourceable accession numbers; even when correct, the answer cannot be audit-trailed by a downstream agent.

alphaCategories.name: Share-Class CUSIP Disambiguation
alphaCategories.description: Berkshire BRK-A and BRK-B are separate CUSIPs (084670108 vs 084670702) with separately disclosed institutional ownership. Free LLMs conflate them. Helm13F keeps them on distinct CUSIPs and returns separate deltas; the resolver maps EDGAR's HEI/A → HEI-A and LEN/B → LEN-B share-class notation to the schema-conformant Yahoo/Google convention.

upstreamGaps.gap: WhaleWisdom / Dataroma / Stockzoa / free EDGAR are dashboard-shaped. None expose a typed API that returns 'who newly bought NVDA, weighted by pct-of-book, ranked' as a single structured response. WhaleWisdom Premium ($300-500/yr) requires manual navigation across multiple screens.
upstreamGaps.howToolFills: Helm13F returns one structured envelope per question with rows + summaryStats + clusterSignal + evidence.sourceRefs + freshness + confidence. Agents compose this into a downstream summary with zero parsing of HTML dashboards. A FinTwit user writing a 'Burry just filed' thread cuts manual delta-and-summary work to one call.

upstreamGaps.gap: Capital IQ and FactSet have the same data inside enterprise terminals priced in the thousands per seat per year. The non-desk audience (FinTwit, independent analysts, newsletter writers, prosumer value investors) has zero access. Desk users would prefer one tool call over navigating menus.
upstreamGaps.howToolFills: $0.10 per response vs $thousands/year per seat. Same underlying SEC EDGAR source; the value is in the pre-computed pct-of-book + conviction tier + cluster detection that Capital IQ surfaces as separate dashboard tabs requiring assembly.

upstreamGaps.gap: ChatGPT and other free LLMs are well-documented to hallucinate fund holdings and have stale training-data 13F snapshots. They cannot compute pctOfBook (no live book values) or run the cluster detection across a curated roster (cannot enumerate the roster).
upstreamGaps.howToolFills: Every Helm13F response is grounded in EDGAR accession numbers; the evidence.facts[] array carries the SEC accession behind each numeric claim. Zero prose hallucination — failure mode is 'no_data_for_quarter' returned cleanly, not invented numbers.
